title: GPU quant + network quick tasks
body:
Daily scratchpad — mixed notes, commands, and tiny checklists. Quick brain dump for the evening shift (short, actionable).

Context: running a small quantization trial for 2.7B model on g4dn-like nodes. Saw weird slowdown correlated with network hiccups while KV cache warms. Need to isolate whether batching or TCP retransmits are the culprit.

Morning summary:
- 09:10: deployed quant build q-v0.3 to canary pool (3 nodes).
- 11:40: observed 20-30ms p99 bump for short sequences (<=64) when KV cache miss rate spiked.
- 12:00: found kernel logs showing occasional 500ms stalls during remote parameter fetch (suspect network).

Immediate checks (today):
- [ ] Re-run q-v0.3 with lower batch size (batch_limit=4) on same canary to see if p99 improves. Priority: high.
- [ ] Simulate packet loss (tc netem 0.5% on canary) and measure token latency delta. Collect tcpdump for 30m. Owner: Jamal.
- [ ] Validate NFS mounts used for model cache; ensure no lock contention (lsof + fuser on /mnt/model-cache).
- [ ] Check kernel stack traces on stalled node: /var/crash/serve-stall-*.log.

Commands / quick snippets to run:
- ssh rnode-03 && sudo tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem loss 0.5% delay 10ms || true
- sudo perf top -p $(pgrep serve-runtime) --call-graph
- sudo tail -n 200 /var/log/serve/kernel.log | grep -i retransmit

Observations to record for the postmortem:
- Node rnode-03 had elevated NIC errors ~11:37 (ifconfig RX errors ++). Check dmesg for ixgbe* messages.
- Disk IOPS normal during the window — rules out cold disk.
- Quantized model showed slightly higher memory usage (KV cache entries larger due to different layout) — could affect GC cycles.

Notes-to-self (ideas / hypotheses):
- Hypothesis A: small network hiccups cause RPC stall which stalls the main event loop; batching aggregates are sensitive at low batch sizes.
- Hypothesis B: quant kernel path increases CPU busy time briefly, exposing latent network buffer exhaustion on node with heavy egress.

Follow-ups & tickets:
- Create a short Linear ticket with attachment of tcpdump + perf samples from rnode-03 (link to attach after upload).
- Assign INFRA-4821 to Jamal for netem experiment and attach results.
- Add a short test in CI: stress-quant + induced 50ms network jitter, run 500 requests, assert p95 < 150ms. Low-effort smoke guard.

Quick checklist for tomorrow morning handoff:
- Paste perf profile link in #infra-ops (start with p95 snapshot)
- Upload tcpdump to S3 under s3://redwood-temp/infra-dumps/maya/2026-03-12/
- If netem reproduces stall, escalate to hardware team to run NIC diagnostics on rnode-03.

Open questions (unsorted):
- Is the KV cache using shared memory or per-process mmap? If shared, any lock contention metrics?
- Could flow-control in our GRPC client be delaying token emission when remote reads are slow? (Check send window stats).
- Should we try a lightweight RDMA test between nodes to rule out virtualized network path issues?

Random notes / TODOs I might forget:
- Ask Priya about schedule for dedicated GPU pool expansion this quarter — might move canary to dedicated hosts.
- Keep an eye on cluster-level autoscaler logs; there was a recent bump in pod churn that coincided with the incidents.
- Consider a temporary fallback: pin canary to a non-quant model variant if stalls persist during business hours.

End-of-day quick timeline (for handoff):
- 09:10 q-v0.3 canary deploy
- 11:37 first p99 jump observed
- 12:05 netem experiment plan drafted
- 12:40 collected initial perf/tcpdump artifacts

If I don't get to everything tonight: prioritize the netem sim + perf capture.
